title: Origin of Jawed Vertebrates
summary: Jawed vertebrates, or gnathostomes, first appear definitively in the Silurian period (444-416 million years ago). Around 420 million years ago, seas were dominated by jawless, armoured fishes, but once jaws evolved, jawed animals diversified rapidly and by the end of the Devonian had largely replaced them. A 419-million-year-old placoderm from Qujing in Yunnan, Entelognathus, already had a modern bony-fish type of jaw, linking placoderms to bony fishes. More than 99 percent of living vertebrates, humans included, have jaws.

uncertainty.note: Silurian gnathostome origins span from early Silurian isolated microremains (~439 Ma) to major diversification and articulated macrofossils in the Ludlow/Pridoli (~423–419 Ma).
